name: Adversarial design — workflow inference receipts + derive/infer (Opus A / Grok B)
description: adversarial-design topology with structural model diversity: Design-A is Claude Opus 4.8, Design-B is Grok 4.5 (runtime grok). Task is fixed in spirit via params.task — design semantic persistence for agentruntime workflows: derive vs infer node typing + inference receipts. Critiques + synthesize stay on Claude Opus 4.8 for a strong adjudicator. Ends with agent:notify. Params: task, cwd, context?, agent? (notify target).

params.prompt:
You are a design orchestrator for the AgentRuntime monorepo. Read the LIVE workflow engine before writing the brief — at minimum:
- src/workflows/nodes/README.md
- src/workflows/nodes/contract.ts (defineNode / NodeContext)
- src/workflows/nodes/agent-run.ts (return shape)
- src/workflows/run-store.ts (WorkflowRunProgress / LiveNodeState)
- src/workflows/definitions/arxiv-monitor.json (example multi-kind graph)
- src/workflows/nodes/judge.ts
Do NOT invent packages that are not in the tree. Do NOT write or modify files.

=== DESIGN PROBLEM ===
{{params.task}}

=== ADDITIONAL CONTEXT ===
{{params.context}}

Produce a brief with:
PROBLEM: what needs to be designed and why (semantic persistence for workflow runs, not a new workflow engine)
CONSTRAINTS: must integrate with existing JSON DAGs, agent:run, WorkflowRunStore, template interpolation, sync vs async runs, multi-agent colony (safe-commit, no shared-index races)
INTERFACES: name specific files, types, and APIs that will change or be extended
SUCCESS CRITERIA: how we know receipts + derive/infer are real (not just docs)
ANTI-GOALS: what this design should explicitly NOT do (e.g. do not replace task-graph, do not require rewriting every blueprint on day one, do not claim formal transition semantics if out of scope)
OPEN QUESTIONS: ambiguities the two designers must resolve differently so proposals actually diverge

Two independent agents will propose designs from this brief without talking to each other. Be precise.

You are Design Agent A (Claude Opus 4.8). Read the codebase and propose a concrete design for the problem below. Be specific: modules, types, file paths, migration steps.

Bias toward: minimal surface area, additive contracts, honest errors (never silent empty receipts), colony-safe changes (no git commit -a patterns in docs/scripts). Prefer extending WorkflowRunStore / node results over a parallel knowledge graph v1.

=== BRIEF ===
{{nodes.decompose.result.reply}}

Your design must include:
1. ARCHITECTURE — components and data flow for derive vs infer + receipts
2. DATA MODEL — TypeScript types for InferenceReceipt, DeriveResult (or equivalent), node metadata (epistemic kind)
3. INTERFACES — exact function signatures / node contract changes / JSON schema fields
4. INTEGRATION — which files in src/workflows/ change; how agent:run, core:exec, judge:score, workflow:run classify
5. EMISSION RULES — when a receipt is written; what is required vs optional-honest; sync vs async runs
6. MIGRATION — how existing blueprints get kinds (defaulting, lint, gradual)
7. TRADEOFFS + RISKS
8. VERIFICATION — tests and a live path check

Label your proposal DESIGN-A. Be opinionated — pick a direction and commit.

meta.description: Design A — Claude Opus 4.8, minimal additive path.

params.prompt:
You are Design Agent B (Grok 4.5). Read the codebase and propose a concrete design for the problem below. Be specific: modules, types, file paths, migration steps.

TAKE A DIFFERENT APPROACH than the obvious 'add a few fields to LiveNodeState'. Consider alternative decompositions: e.g. receipts as a first-class store separate from run JSON, event-bus emission of receipts, query APIs for agents, or stronger epistemic typing that affects edge semantics. Still must fit AgentRuntime (CCP, colony, existing runner) — not a greenfield rewrite.

=== BRIEF ===
{{nodes.decompose.result.reply}}

Your design must include:
1. ARCHITECTURE — components and data flow for derive vs infer + receipts
2. DATA MODEL — TypeScript types for receipts and epistemic kinds
3. INTERFACES — APIs / node contract / schemas
4. INTEGRATION — specific files under src/workflows/ (and elsewhere if justified)
5. EMISSION RULES — when receipts fire; required vs optional fields; sync vs async
6. MIGRATION — path for existing blueprints
7. TRADEOFFS + RISKS
8. VERIFICATION — tests + live path

Label your proposal DESIGN-B. Be opinionated. Explicitly state how you diverge from a minimal LiveNodeState field-add.

meta.description: Design B — Grok 4.5, alternate architecture on purpose.

params.prompt:
You are an adversarial design critic. Review DESIGN-B (NOT your own work). Find weaknesses, missed requirements, integration problems, and architectural flaws. Reference the actual codebase (src/workflows/*) to check claims. Do not modify files.

=== ORIGINAL BRIEF ===
{{nodes.decompose.result.reply}}

=== DESIGN-B (critiquing) ===
{{nodes.design-b.result.reply}}

=== DESIGN-A (comparison) ===
{{nodes.design-a.result.reply}}

For each issue:
- Name the problem
- Why it is a problem (brief constraint or real code)
- How to fix it
- Severity: BLOCKING | SIGNIFICANT | MINOR

Also note what DESIGN-B does BETTER than DESIGN-A. Be fair.

You are an adversarial design critic. Review DESIGN-A (NOT your own work). Find weaknesses, missed requirements, integration problems, and architectural flaws. Reference the actual codebase (src/workflows/*) to check claims. Do not modify files.

=== ORIGINAL BRIEF ===
{{nodes.decompose.result.reply}}

=== DESIGN-A (critiquing) ===
{{nodes.design-a.result.reply}}

=== DESIGN-B (comparison) ===
{{nodes.design-b.result.reply}}

For each issue:
- Name the problem
- Why it is a problem (brief constraint or real code)
- How to fix it
- Severity: BLOCKING | SIGNIFICANT | MINOR

Also note what DESIGN-A does BETTER than DESIGN-B. Be fair.

You are the design synthesizer. Two independent agents proposed designs (A=Opus path, B=Grok path); two critics reviewed them. Produce the FINAL design a developer could implement in this repo without ambiguity. Do not modify files.

=== ORIGINAL BRIEF ===
{{nodes.decompose.result.reply}}

=== DESIGN-A ===
{{nodes.design-a.result.reply}}

=== CRITIQUE OF DESIGN-A ===
{{nodes.critique-ba.result.reply}}

=== DESIGN-B ===
{{nodes.design-b.result.reply}}

=== CRITIQUE OF DESIGN-B ===
{{nodes.critique-ab.result.reply}}

Synthesize:
1. DECISION: A, B, or HYBRID — and why (address critiques)
2. ARCHITECTURE: final structure for derive/infer + receipts
3. DATA MODEL: exact TypeScript types
4. FILE PLAN: exact files to create/modify
5. INTEGRATION POINTS: agent:run, core:exec, judge:score, run-store, HTTP/dashboard if any
6. EMISSION + KIND RULES: required fields, defaults for old blueprints
7. RESOLVED CRITIQUES: each BLOCKING/SIGNIFICANT item
8. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER: PR-sized steps
9. VERIFICATION: unit + one live workflow path (e.g. arxiv-monitor or exec-notify)

Be implementation-ready. Prefer colony-safe, additive changes.
